# Cogito

> Cogito is a self-hosted API key pool. It stores many API keys per provider (SerpAPI, ElevenLabs, or any API key based HTTP service), hands out a working key on demand, detects rate limits and quota exhaustion, cools keys down and rotates to the next one. Agents use it either as a proxy (Cogito injects the key, the secret is never exposed) or by leasing a key and reporting the outcome.

Base URL is wherever Cogito is deployed, for example `http://localhost:8080`. All consumer calls need an app token (`cog_...`) created in the dashboard. All bodies are JSON. Errors look like `{"error": {"code": "string", "message": "string"}}`.

Key facts for agents:

- Prefer proxy mode. Call `/proxy/{service}/{provider path}` exactly as you would call the provider, minus the provider key. Cogito retries with the next key on rate limits.
- Use lease mode only when you must hold the raw key (for example a provider SDK). Always report the outcome so bad keys cool down, and so the key's concurrency slot is released (see below).
- HTTP 503 with code `no_key_available` means every key is cooling down or exhausted. Wait `retry_after_sec` seconds.
- HTTP 503 with code `all_keys_busy` means usable keys exist but every one is at its concurrency limit. It clears as soon as another caller reports; retry after `retry_after_sec` (usually 1) or lease with `wait_sec`.
- An app may be limited to some services and to mode `proxy`, `lease` or `both`. Call `GET /api/v1/services` to see what you can use.
- Report every lease within 10 minutes of `expires_at`. A second report gets 409, a late one 410.
- HTTP 503 with code `service_unavailable` means the provider itself keeps failing and Cogito paused traffic to it (circuit breaker). Wait `retry_after_sec`.
- HTTP 429 with code `app_limit_reached` means your app used up its daily or monthly request or budget limit. `reset_at` says when it lifts.
- `{service}` can also be a service group: Cogito tries each member service in order and moves on when one has no usable key, is down, or runs out of keys. `X-Cogito-Service` says which member answered.

## Auth

- `Authorization: Bearer cog_...` (preferred), or `X-Cogito-Token: cog_...`.
- Proxy only: query parameter `?cogito_token=cog_...` for tools that only accept a URL.
- Cogito strips all three before forwarding upstream.

## Concurrency limits

- A key can have a concurrency limit: how many requests may use it at once. Each service has a default (`max_concurrency`, 0 means unlimited) that a key can override. ElevenLabs defaults to 2 per key.
- On a service with a limit, a lease is exclusive: it holds one of the key's slots until it is reported (`POST /api/v1/leases/{lease_id}/report`) or expires (`ttl_sec`, default 120s on limited services, 300s otherwise). An unreported lease blocks the slot until then, so always report, on success and on failure.
- `POST /api/v1/lease` accepts `wait_sec` (0 to 60): wait up to that long for a slot when every usable key is busy, instead of failing at once with `all_keys_busy`.
- Proxy mode handles this for you: requests queue for up to the service `queue_timeout_sec` (ElevenLabs default 30s) and never exceed the limit in parallel on one key. When the queue wait runs out the proxy answers 503 `all_keys_busy`.

## Consumer API

- [GET /api/v1/services](/llms-full.txt#get-apiv1services): services this token may use, with `available`, `base_url` and `auth` `{type, name, prefix}`.
- [POST /api/v1/lease](/llms-full.txt#post-apiv1lease): body `{"service": "serpapi", "exclude_key_ids": [], "ttl_sec": 300, "wait_sec": 0}`, returns `{"lease_id", "key_id", "service", "secret", "auth": {"type", "name", "prefix"}, "base_url", "expires_at"}` (put `prefix` before the secret when present), or 503 `{"error": {"code": "no_key_available"}, "retry_after_sec": n}` or 503 `{"error": {"code": "all_keys_busy"}, "retry_after_sec": 1}`.
- [POST /api/v1/leases/{lease_id}/report](/llms-full.txt#post-apiv1leaseslease_idreport): body `{"outcome", "status_code", "retry_after_sec", "message", "rotate"}`, returns `{"ok": true, "next": <lease or null>}`. With `rotate: true`, `next` is a fresh lease on another key.
- [ANY /proxy/{service}/{path}](/llms-full.txt#any-proxyservicepath): forwards to `base_url/{path}` with query string and body, injecting a key. Methods GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS. Response headers add `X-Cogito-Key-Id`, `X-Cogito-Attempts` and `X-Cogito-Service`. Redirects are returned to you, not followed. On services with caching, identical GETs are answered from cache (`X-Cogito-Cache: hit`, no quota spent); send `Cache-Control: no-cache` to skip it. Send `Idempotency-Key: <id>` to make retries safe: a repeat within 10 minutes replays the first response (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`).
- [GET /healthz](/llms-full.txt#public-endpoints): `{"ok": true, "version": "..."}`, no auth.

## Outcomes

- `ok`: call succeeded, resets the key's failure counter.
- `rate_limited`: key cools down for `retry_after_sec` (at most 24h), or exponential backoff from the service cooldown, capped at 1h.
- `busy`: the account is at its concurrency limit. The key steps aside for `retry_after_sec` (default 1s) without backoff.
- `quota_exhausted`: key parked as `exhausted` until its quota resets (or 24h).
- `invalid`: key marked `invalid` and removed from rotation.
- `banned`: the provider suspended the account. Key marked `banned`; only an operator reset brings it back.
- `error`: provider or network failure that is not the key's fault. Key is not penalized.

## Proxy examples

- [SerpAPI search](/llms-full.txt#serpapi): `GET /proxy/serpapi/search.json?engine=google&q=coffee` with `Authorization: Bearer cog_...`. Do not send `api_key`.
- [ElevenLabs text to speech](/llms-full.txt#elevenlabs): `POST /proxy/elevenlabs/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}` with JSON `{"text": "Hello", "model_id": "eleven_multilingual_v2"}` and `Accept: audio/mpeg`. Do not send `xi-api-key`.

## MCP

- [POST /mcp](/llms-full.txt#mcp): MCP streamable HTTP endpoint (JSON responses), same app token auth. Tools: `list_services`, `get_key` (accepts `ttl_sec` and `wait_sec`), `report_key`, `pool_status`, `proxy_request`.

## SDKs

Every SDK's lease call and `with_key` helper accept the wait option (`wait_sec` in Python, PHP and Ruby, `waitSec` in TypeScript, `LeaseOptions.Wait` / `WithWait` in Go) and raise a distinct busy error that still counts as "no key available" (`AllKeysBusy`, `AllKeysBusyError`, or `ErrNoKeyAvailable` with `Busy` in Go). `with_key` always reports its leases.

- [Python](/llms-full.txt#python): `pip install cogito-keys`, then `from cogito import Cogito`.
- [TypeScript and JavaScript](/llms-full.txt#typescript-and-javascript): `npm install @cogito/keys`, then `import { Cogito } from "@cogito/keys"`. Node 18+, Bun, Deno, browsers.
- [Go](/llms-full.txt#go): `go get github.com/cogito-keys/cogito-go`, package `cogito`.
- [PHP](/llms-full.txt#php): `composer require cogito/keys`, class `Cogito\Cogito`.
- [Ruby](/llms-full.txt#ruby): `gem install cogito-keys`, then `require "cogito"`.

## Admin API and CLI

Operators can script the admin API with a token from Settings, API tokens (`Authorization: Bearer cogadm_...`, scope `read`, `write` or `admin`, never above the creator's role). The same binary ships a client: `cogito ctl login https://cogito.example --token cogadm_...`, then `cogito ctl status`, `services`, `keys <service>`, `keys add <service> < keys.txt`, `keys check <service>`, `events`, `breaker <service> [--reset]`, `cache purge <service>`, `usage <app-id>`.
